To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of ICT in education in the Netherlands is still in its infancy; (2) there are a number of factors, both on the supply and demand side, which have an effect on the use of ICT; (3) the use of the Internet is more widespread than that of CD-ROM; (4) the use of CD-ROM is more widespread than the use of other ICT; (5) the use of all forms of ICT is more widespread in the vocational training sector

(1) the number of students who use the Internet for learning purposes is still relatively low, (2) the Internet is used more often for learning purposes by students who have more experience in using the Internet, (3) there are significant differences between students with regard to the use of the Internet for learning, (4) there are differences between the different groups of students in the way they use the Internet for their learning, (5) the Internet is more often used by students who are more motivated
In summary, our research is concerned with
how ICT is being used to support learning and teaching in higher education and how it is perceived by lecturers and students.
the following issues: (a) What is the impact of the introduction of ICT on the demand for education and on the demand for training?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, on average, the costs and benefits of e-learning are about the same as the costs and benefits for traditional face-to-face training.
there is no conclusive evidence that e-learning is more effective than classroom teaching, but also that there is no evidence that e-learning does not work.
the use of ICT for education and training is a complex phenomenon, which is not only dependent upon the availability of the technology, but also on the way it is used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICT has a significant impact on the quality of education.

we have been able to show that the effects of the ICT-based learning environment on student achievement are small and not statistically significant, but that the effects on student engagement are larger and statistically significant.
the Internet has become a major force in education, and that it is changing the way we think of education.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the Internet can be used to provide training and education, there are still a number of barriers to be overcome.
the impact of ICT on education and learning can be substantial.
the impact of ICT on the labour market is not as simple as some have argued.
